text:
sam: heads-up — canary token/sec dropped ~30% after the merge that went out at 09:12.
sam: saw it on the perf dashboard, but local microbenchmarks don't show the same degradation.
sam: attaching the graph: https://perf.internal/redwood/canary/1766
jena: omg, saw the alert. which merge? any PR number?
sam: merge commit 9f3b2a1 — it includes the scheduler heuristics refactor + kernel selection fallback.
oliver: scheduler refactor rings a bell. we changed target_batch_size calc to factor in kv_cache hit ratio, could that cause underfill?
jena: possible — if kv hits are lower than the estimator expects, batcher could be throttling to smaller batches and increasing qdelay.
rachel: I ran top-down profiling on an affected canary pod. Main hotspot is scheduler.wait_loop (scheduling queue) and then context switch spikes when forming batches.
jena: can you paste the flamegraph snippet?
rachel: ```
# flamegraph excerpt
scheduler.wait_loop  45%
  batch_builder.form_batches  30%
    kv_cache.lookup  10%
    kernel_selector.choose  8%
    io_wait  12%
```
oliver: kernel_selector.choose at 8% is higher than expected — we changed kernel scoring to prefer memory-bound kernels for long sequences in that patch.
sam: my hypothesis: kernel scoring change picked a slower path on our typical short-chat seqs, and batcher then underfilled because the runtime estimated longer exec times.
jena: that would explain token/sec drop and increased queuing. Any CI perf job failing before rollout?
perf-ci-bot: [perf/canary] regression detected: token/s -28% vs baseline on commit 9f3b2a1. Details: https://ci.redwood/Perf/1766
rachel: good catch — CI flagged it but the release pipeline silenced perf alerts because the release window had manual approval.
sam: can we bisect quickly? suspecting either scheduler change (PR #4132) or kernel scoring tweak (PR #4189).
oliver: I'll run a quick bisect on canary by toggling kernel scoring to previous strategy. If that restores token/s, we know where to revert.
jena: also check KV cache invalidation logic in #4132 — if we changed when entries are considered stale, kv hit ratio could drop and feed bad numbers to the batcher.
oliver: running test now locally against canary image with older kernel selector.
deploy-bot: Rollout halted for service "runtime-canary" — operator hold by sam
sam: holding rollout for prod until we confirm root cause. no further rollouts.
oliver: quick update: swapping kernel selector back to legacy reduces per-request latency by ~22% locally. pushing a patch to CI now (build 176600).
jena: great. can we also add diagnostic counters for batcher: estimated_exec_ms vs actual_exec_ms and kv_hit_ratio in the next hotfix so we can trace mismatch?
sam: yes plz. if bisect confirms kernel change, prefer reverting kernel scoring first and then follow-up with metric additions.
rachel: adding to today's oncall checklist: capture tail-latency traces + per-batch kernel decisions. I'll open an issue with logs: https://issues.redwood/RE-842
oliver: CI run completed: token/s back to baseline on branch with legacy kernel selector. attaching diff for quick revert: https://git.redwood/revert/4189
sam: ok let's revert 4189 from canary and re-run canary perf gating. If stable, then we'll merge small metric additions and rework kernel scoring offline.
jena: adding a canary checkpoint: do not auto-continue rollout if perf regression > 10% for 30m.
perf-ci-bot: [perf-gate] canary reverted to previous kernel selector. New run shows token/s within ±3% baseline.
sam: thanks everyone. follow-up: rachel + jena + oliver to draft postmortem + mitigations. I'll keep prod rollout paused until we have metrics in place.
rachel: will do — will include a suggested fix for batcher estimator to fall back to observed running averages when kv_hit_ratio variance is high.
oliver: note for later: consider separating kernel scoring decisions by sequence_length buckets rather than global heuristics.
sam: cool. closing this thread once the revert is promoted and metrics land. :thumbsup:
